strings.name: Mohamed ElBaradei
strings.summary: ElBaradei moved from legal education and Egyptian diplomacy to the IAEA, serving as director general from 1997 to 2009 through Iraq inspections and disputes over Iran and North Korea. He shared the 2005 Nobel Peace Prize with the agency. He later advocated Egyptian political reform, briefly serving as interim vice president in 2013 before resigning over the deadly protest dispersals, and continued international advocacy.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education

strings.highlights.h1.title: Verification and nonproliferation
strings.highlights.h1.text: Led IAEA safeguards and nuclear diplomacy against military misuse of nuclear energy.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Peace prize and public politics
strings.highlights.h2.text: Shared the 2005 peace prize with the IAEA, later pursuing Egyptian reform and resigning over violent protest dispersals.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Resigned interim vice presidency
strings.timeline.t1.text: Resigned in protest at deadly dispersals of pro-Morsi sit-ins.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Advocated Egyptian reform
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became a public opposition figure during anti-Mubarak protests and political transition.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Ended IAEA tenure
strings.timeline.t3.text: Completed three terms as IAEA director general.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Shared Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t4.text: Shared the prize with the IAEA for preventing military misuse and promoting safe peaceful nuclear energy.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Led IAEA
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Hans Blix as director general.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined IAEA secretariat
strings.timeline.t6.text: Served as legal adviser and later led external relations.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Completed international-law doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned a doctorate in international law at NYU.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Began diplomatic service
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined Egypt’s foreign ministry and later served at UN missions.
